best-broadway-shows.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows in March 2026

March 2026 finds Broadway in a remarkable moment of creative diversity, with the Great White Way offering everything from revolutionary hip-hop musicals to whimsical robot romances and absurdist historical farces. This month's top-rated shows span decades of theatrical innovation, proving that both new voices and established classics continue to captivate critics and audiences alike.

Leading the rankings is **Hamilton**, which remains a groundbreaking force in American theater with its hip-hop retelling of the founding fathers' story. The show continues to set the standard for how musicals can reimagine history through contemporary musical forms. Close behind, **Maybe Happy Ending** emerges as one of Broadway's most original new musicals, earning widespread acclaim for its unexpectedly moving story about two robots finding connection. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!** delivers something entirely different—Cole Escola's riotous reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist has become one of the season's most talked-about productions.

The current lineup demonstrates Broadway's remarkable range, with long-running spectacles like **The Lion King** and **The Book of Mormon** holding their own against fresh arrivals and timely revivals like **Ragtime**. The average critic score of 83/100 across these ten productions reflects a particularly strong theatrical season, where audiences can find excellence whether they're drawn to family-friendly Disney magic, boundary-pushing comedy, or emotionally resonant drama.

Whether you're a first-time theatergoer or a seasoned Broadway veteran, March 2026 offers an exceptional array of critically acclaimed productions worth experiencing live.

Leading the pack, **Hamilton** continues to prove why it transformed the American musical, with critics still celebrating Lin-Manuel Rodrigo's hip-hop retelling of the founding fathers' story as essential theater. Close behind, **Maybe Happy Ending** has emerged as one of the season's most pleasant surprises—this tender robot love story demonstrates that Broadway can still deliver genuinely original concepts that resonate emotionally with audiences and critics alike.

The current landscape reflects Broadway's diversity of offerings. Long-running spectacles like **The Lion King** remind audiences why Julie Taymor's visual artistry remains unmatched, while **Ragtime**'s timely revival speaks to contemporary America through its early 20th-century lens, powered by Joshua Henry's acclaimed performance. Meanwhile, **Hadestown** continues its folk-opera reimagining of Greek mythology, and **The Book of Mormon** proves that sharp satire still has a home on Broadway.

Rounding out the top ten, perennial favorites **Chicago** and **SIX** offer contrasting takes on entertainment—one a cynical jazz-age satire, the other an exuberant pop celebration.

Whether you're drawn to groundbreaking innovation, spectacular stagecraft, or pure entertainment, this month's top-rated shows offer compelling reasons to experience live musical theater.

These productions, which debuted in the brief window before the industry's historic shutdown, have since become notable touchstones in Broadway history—some returning for extended runs, others living on primarily through their critical reception and cultural impact.

Among the standout productions from this cohort, **Les Misérables** leads with its grittier reimagining at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely embrace its darker interpretation of the beloved musical. **A Soldier's Play** follows closely, marking the long-overdue Broadway debut of Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama in a stellar revival that proves the work's examination of race and power remains urgently relevant decades after it was written.

The year also brought more divisive fare: Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** splits critics between those captivated by her luminous performance and those who find the adaptation's theatrical translation lacking. Similarly, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining provokes strong reactions, with its bold visual design and fresh approach either thrilling or alienating audiences depending on their appetite for deconstruction.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 demonstrates Broadway's continued willingness to take risks—from experimental revivals to intimate literary adaptations—even as commercial pressures mount. For theatergoers interested in understanding this pivotal moment in Broadway history, these productions offer essential viewing and context for the evolution that followed.

Solo performances particularly distinguished this season, with **Lackawanna Blues** and **Is This a Room** demonstrating how powerful minimalist theater can be. The latter transforms a verbatim FBI transcript into gripping drama, while the former showcases virtuosic character work.

With an average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, 2021's Broadway offerings maintained remarkably high quality during a period of uncertainty. Whether you're drawn to experimental docudrama, reimagined classics, or exuberant new musicals like **SIX**, these shows represent essential chapters in Broadway's ongoing story.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater just before—and in some cases, just after—the pandemic transformed the industry. These five productions, averaging a solid 74/100 critical score, showcase the range of dramatic storytelling that defined the season.

**Les Misérables** leads our rankings at 83/100, with critics largely embracing this grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, though the reimagined approach doesn't win over all traditionalists. The production demonstrates how classic material continues to find new resonance through bold directorial choices.

**A Soldier's Play** earns the second spot with 78/100 across 29 reviews, marking a powerful and long-overdue Broadway debut for Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama. This stellar revival proves the work's examination of race, power, and identity within a 1940s military base remains devastatingly relevant decades after its premiere.

The remaining three shows reflect the diversity of 2020's theatrical offerings: Laura Linney's luminous solo performance in **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics despite widespread admiration for her work, while **Grand Horizons** delivers pleasant if familiar boulevard comedy elevated by Jane Alexander's performance. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves characteristically divisive, with striking video design and visceral staging choices that either thrill or alienate depending on the viewer.

Whether you're revisiting these productions or discovering them for the first time, each offers a distinct perspective on what American theater looked like at a pivotal cultural moment.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the 2021 Broadway season stands as a watershed moment—the year theater roared back to life after the pandemic shutdown. The shows that opened during this period captured both the industry's resilience and its creative ambition, with productions ranging from intimate experimental works to grand spectacles.

Leading our rankings is **Dana H.**, an unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's extraordinary lip-sync performance. This daring production exemplifies the bold theatrical experiments that emerged during Broadway's reopening. Close behind, **The Phantom of the Opera** reminds us that Lloyd Webber's mega-musical remained a cornerstone of the Broadway landscape, while **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** demonstrates how classic material can be radically reimagined through immersive staging.

The 2021 season showcased remarkable diversity in storytelling approaches. Verbatim theater found powerful expression in **Is This a Room**, transforming an FBI transcript into gripping drama. Solo performances proved equally compelling, with **Lackawanna Blues** and its virtuosic character work. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy** offered epic scope, and gender-swapped revivals like **Company** breathed new life into canonical works.

With an average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the 2021 season delivered consistently strong work during an uncertain time. From Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's **Pass Over**—chosen to reopen Broadway—to Lynn Nottage's compassionate **Clyde's** and the pop-fueled energy of **SIX**, these shows captured a moment when theater felt more essential than ever.

Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting favorites, this guide offers a comprehensive look at the year Broadway came back.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable period of theatrical achievement, with an impressive roster of shows continuing to resonate with audiences years after their debuts.

The season's crown jewel is **Kimberly Akimbo**, which earns the highest critical acclaim with a score of 88/100. Critics consistently hail David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori's musical as a near-perfect achievement, masterfully balancing quirky humor with profound emotional depth. Close behind, **Into the Woods** (86/100) delivers a triumphant stripped-down revival that serves as a fitting tribute to Stephen Sondheim's genius, while **A Strange Loop** (86/100) matches that score with Michael R. Jackson's brazenly original, Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical that critics praise for its brutal honesty and theatrical innovation.

The collection showcases an extraordinary concentration of Pulitzer Prize winners, including Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog**, Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt**, and three contemporary Pulitzer-winning dramas: **Between Riverside and Crazy**, **How I Learned to Drive**, and **Cost of Living**. This clustering of award-winning work reflects a season that prioritized substantive storytelling and theatrical excellence.

With an average critic score of 83/100 across all ten featured productions, the 2022 season demonstrates consistent quality alongside remarkable range—from intimate solo performances like Mike Birbiglia's **The Old Man & The Pool** to audacious satire in **Ain't No Mo'**. Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting familiar favorites, this collection represents some of the most critically celebrated theater of the decade.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2023 continue to demonstrate exceptional artistic achievement, with our featured selections averaging an impressive 82/100 critical score. This vintage represents a particularly strong year for dramatic theater, encompassing everything from long-overdue revivals to innovative new works.

Leading the rankings is Maria Friedman's acclaimed revival of **Merrily We Roll Along** (85/100), which has successfully rehabilitated Sondheim's infamous 1981 flop into a critically celebrated triumph. The production earns praise for its emotionally resonant interpretation that finally unlocks the show's potential. Tied at the top is **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** (85/100), a West End transfer that surprises critics by transcending its source material with technically stunning stagecraft that works as compelling theater beyond mere fan service.

Close behind, **Appropriate** (83/100) stands out as a searing contemporary family drama, with Sarah Paulson anchoring what critics describe as a blistering ensemble performance in what many consider a modern masterpiece. The year also saw significant revivals of classics, including **Purlie Victorious** (82/100), Ossie Davis's 1961 satire finally receiving its long-overdue Broadway return with bracingly relevant humor, and **Parade** (82/100), whose timely themes resonate powerfully through Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond's powerhouse performances.

The 2023 season's diversity extends from Alex Edelman's solo comedy **Just for Us** (81/100) to the Pulitzer Prize-winning **Fat Ham** (80/100), demonstrating Broadway's range across theatrical forms and voices. Whether you're seeking classic musical revivals, urgent contemporary drama, or innovative new writing, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theater.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As of March 2026, the Broadway shows that premiered in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. The class of 2024 brought an eclectic mix of original works, inventive musicals, and reimagined classics that collectively earned an impressive 85/100 average critic score.

Leading the pack is **La Llamada**, though with limited reviews, followed closely by **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's meticulously crafted drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio. Critics have embraced it as a theatrical marvel, celebrating its authentic portrayal of the creative process and the tensions that fuel artistic collaboration. The production's attention to period detail and emotional nuance has made it one of the season's most discussed works.

**Operation Mincemeat** represents another 2024 success story, transferring from grassroots origins to Broadway with its inventive energy intact. The ensemble-driven musical about a World War II deception operation has won over critics with its clever staging and infectious spirit. Meanwhile, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as one of Broadway's most original musicals in recent memory—a robot love story that manages to be both whimsical and deeply affecting.

The year also brought Cole Escola's **Oh, Mary!**, an absurdist reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln that has become a word-of-mouth phenomenon, alongside respected revivals of **Gypsy** starring Audra McDonald and a lavish new **Oliver!** These productions showcase 2024 as a year when Broadway successfully balanced bold new voices with fresh takes on beloved classics.

Whether you're drawn to innovative storytelling, powerhouse performances, or reimagined standards, the 2024 Broadway season offers compelling options still running strong in 2026.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway moves into spring 2026, the plays that opened last year continue to demonstrate the enduring power of dramatic storytelling on stage. This month's top 10 plays—averaging a strong 84/100 from critics—showcase remarkable range, from bold contemporary works to reimagined classics that speak urgently to our current moment.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons** (91/100), which critics praise for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. The director's stripped-down approach to Arthur Miller's classic proves that great plays need little embellishment when performed with such raw power. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** (89/100) earns widespread acclaim for its joyous spirit and tender heart, reminding audiences why this quirky musical-comedy hybrid became a beloved favorite.

Family-friendly fare also claims its place among the year's best with **Paddington The Musical** (86/100), where critics consistently marvel at the remarkably lifelike bear puppet that brings the beloved character to theatrical life. Meanwhile, new American plays like Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** (82/100) and Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' **Purpose** (82/100) offer smart, provocative examinations of identity, language, and family dynamics.

The diversity of this year's offerings—from Ivo van Hove's stark modernism to David Yazbek's darkly comic musical storytelling in **Dead Outlaw**—reflects a Broadway season willing to take creative risks while honoring theatrical traditions. Whether you're drawn to classic American drama, intimate character studies, or enchanting family entertainment, these critically acclaimed productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theater this spring.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

As March 2026 unfolds, the Broadway season presents a modest opening quarter for new play productions, with just one entry marking the year's theatrical landscape so far.

**Every Brilliant Thing** stands as the sole new play debut of 2026 to date, earning a critic score of 66 out of 100. The production represents the entirety of this year's fresh dramatic offerings on Broadway, making it a notable if singular data point in what remains an emerging season.

With an average critic score of 66 across the single production featured, the year's theatrical output reflects a measured start rather than a banner beginning. This limited landscape differs considerably from typical Broadway seasons, which generally see multiple play openings competing for audiences and critical attention during the winter and early spring months.

The current theatrical environment suggests that producers and creative teams may be taking a cautious approach to launching new work, or that the traditional Broadway calendar has shifted its patterns. Whether this represents a temporary lull or signals broader changes in how plays are programmed remains to be seen as the year progresses.

For theatergoers seeking new dramatic work on Broadway this March, the options are straightforward but limited. As the spring season develops, additional productions are likely to emerge and reshape the year's offerings. Those interested in experiencing 2026's new plays should monitor announcements for upcoming productions that will expand the current landscape beyond this initial entry.
